notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 09/02/2025
Patient: Lakisha Mills, 84-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 09/02/2025. The study was conducted to evaluate the patient's sleep patterns and identify any sleep-disordered breathing events.

Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 42.6 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 12% of all events. These results indicate severe sleep apnea with a significant component of central and mixed apneas.

Sleep architecture showed normal distribution of sleep stages appropriate for the patient's age. No other significant abnormalities were noted.

In conclusion, the patient has severe sleep apnea as demonstrated by the elevated AHI and the presence of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and treatment planning are recommended.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/10/2026
Patient: Lakisha Mills, 85-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Ms. Mills has a history of obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed several years ago. She has been prescribed CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 28.4 kg/m2.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 2.9 hours per night on 24% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Assessment:
Ms. Mills demonstrates poor adherence to CPAP therapy despite efforts to optimize mask fit and support. Given her intolerance, alternative treatment options should be considered.

Plan:
1. Discuss alternative therapies including positional therapy and oral appliance options.
2. Consider referral to dental sleep specialist for oral appliance evaluation.
3. Continue monitoring symptoms and sleep quality.
4. Follow-up appointment in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Summary:
Ms. Mills is an elderly female with obstructive sleep apnea who is unable to tolerate CPAP therapy. Alternative management strategies will be pursued to improve her sleep quality and overall health.
